extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies and their staff who prepare documents for filing and publication in the Federal Register; Office of the Federal Register and Office of Management and Budget staff involved in routing/clearance
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for preparing, formatting, routing, and filing documents for public inspection and publication in the Federal Register, and for drafting material subject to codification in the Code of Federal Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency schedule request content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency requesting publication on the emergency schedule must briefly describe the emergency and the benefits to be attributed to immediate publication; the request must be made by letter. Documents assigned to the emergency schedule shall be published as soon as possible and will be filed for public inspection on the working day before publication unless emergency filing for public inspection is also requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director assigns a document to the emergency schedule whenever the Director concurs with the request and it is feasible. Requests must be in letter form and explain the emergency and public benefit of immediate publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for emergency filing for public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may request emergency filing for public inspection to provide the fastest possible public access to a document after it has been received, processed, and assigned a publication date. Emergency filing is a special arrangement that deviates from the regular filing schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A document receiving emergency filing stays on public inspection until published according to its publication schedule. Emergency filing may be requested for documents on the regular, emergency, or deferred publication schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timing for emergency filing for public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency requesting emergency filing for public inspection must briefly describe the emergency and benefits to immediate public access by letter. The Director of the Federal Register will approve such requests when the Director concurs and it is feasible. Approved documents shall be filed as soon as possible following processing and scheduling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be by letter; approval depends on Director concurrence and feasibility; filings should occur promptly after processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for deferred schedule assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: A document may be assigned to the deferred schedule when (1) there are technical problems, unusual or lengthy tables or illustrations, or the document's size requires extraordinary processing time, or (2) the agency requests a deferred publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of the Federal Register staff will notify the agency if its documents must be assigned to a deferred schedule. Tabular material may trigger deferred scheduling (§ 18.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originals and copies required
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency submitting a document to be filed and published in the Federal Register shall send an original and two duplicate originals or certified copies. If the document is printed or processed on both sides, one of the copies must be a collated, single-sided copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist for Executive orders and proclamations under § 19.2. Agencies with computer-processed data are urged to consult OFR staff about possible use of the data in publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on combined category documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will not accept a document for filing and publication if it combines material that must appear under more than one category in the Federal Register (e.g., both rulemaking and notice of proposed rulemaking material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where two related documents are to be published in the same Federal Register issue, agencies may insert cross-references in each document instead of combining categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission point and transmittal letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document required by law to be filed for public inspection and published in the Federal Register shall be sent to the Director of the Federal Register. Except for special handling cases, a letter of transmittal is not needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt dates are determined when a signed original and clear and legible copies are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and physical condition of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed or processed document may be accepted for filing and publication if it is on bond or similar quality paper, legible, and free of adhesive or correction tape. Documents in the form of a letter or press release may not be accepted for filing/publication in rules and regulations, proposed rules, or notices categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original documents submitted by telecommunication and authenticated by digital signatures consistent with federal standards and OFR technical specifications may be accepted; consult OFR for pilot projects and technical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified copies or duplicate originals of each document must be submitted with the original. Each copy must be entirely clear and legible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified copies are required except in certain Presidential document contexts; see § 18.6 for certification form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each copy of each document submitted for filing and publication, except a Presidential document or a duplicate original, must be certified with the wording: 'Certified to be a true copy of the original.' The certification must be signed by a certifying officer designated under § 16.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact certification wording and ensure the signatory is an authorized certifying officer per § 16.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The original and each duplicate original document must be signed in ink, with the name and title of the official typing or stamped beneath the signature. Initialed or impressed signatures will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents submitted under telecommunication/digital signature authorities (§ 18.4(c)) may be authenticated by digital signatures consistent with federal standards and OFR technical specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional use of seal
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a seal on an original document or certified copy is optional with the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No mandatory requirement; agencies may elect to use a seal per their practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document submitted for filing and publication shall conform to the current edition of the U.S. Government Printing Office Style Manual in punctuation, capitalization, spelling, and other matters of style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The GPO Style Manual is the authoritative reference for formatting and style; OFR and GPO conventions should be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations, tabular material, and forms format
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is necessary to publish a form or illustration, a clear and legible original form or illustration, or a clear and completely legible reproduction approximately 8 1/2 by 11 inches, shall be included in the original document and each certified copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents that include tabular material may be assigned to the deferred publication schedule (§ 17.7). Charts intended for the Government Manual must be legible when reduced to Manual page size (§ 20.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble requirement and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency submitting a proposed or final rule document for publication shall prepare a preamble that will inform the reader who is not an expert of the basis and purpose for the rule or proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble must be accessible to non-experts and explain why the action is needed and its intended effect; it serves as the explanatory front matter for rule documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble format and required headings
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble shall contain specified headings and information in a fixed format: AGENCY (name), ACTION (type of document), SUMMARY (brief statements in simple language of (i) the action being taken; (ii) circumstances creating the need; (iii) intended effect), DATES (comments, effective date, hearing), ADDRESSES, FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT, and SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION may include background and major issues, differences between final and proposed rules, response to substantive public comments, and any other information the agency considers appropriate. Use the headings on separate lines in the order shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal or correction of filed documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A document filed for public inspection but not yet published may be withdrawn or corrected by the submitting agency. Withdrawals or minor corrections may be made by a timely letter signed by a duly authorized representative; extensive corrections may require agency withdrawal of the document from publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the originally filed document and the withdrawing/correcting letter remain on file and are retained by the Office of the Federal Register after the public inspection period expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of printing errors in the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Typographical or clerical errors made in printing of the Federal Register shall be corrected by insertion of an appropriate notation or reprinting without further agency documentation if the Director determines the error would confuse/mislead the reader or affect text subject to codification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuing agencies must review published documents and notify OFR of printing errors. If the error originated in the agency-submitted document, the agency must prepare and submit a correction document for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of expired regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may reinstate regulations removed from the CFR data base which have expired by their own terms only by republishing the regulations in full text in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires full republication in the Federal Register; mere citation or reference is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and computation of time periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents that include an effective date or time period should either set a date certain or a time period measured by a certain number of days after publication. When a time period is measured by days after publication, OFR staff will compute the date to be inserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counting: the day after publication is counted as one; include Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. If the final count falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday, the date certain will be the next succeeding Federal business day. If effective date depends on Congressional action or court decision that changes the date, the agency must promptly publish a document announcing the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of subjects in agency regulations (index terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency submitting a document published in the Rules and Regulations or Proposed Rules sections shall include a list of index terms for each CFR part affected and place the list as the last item in the Supplementary Information portion of the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies shall use terms contained in the Federal Register Thesaurus of Indexing Terms to prepare the list; additional terms may be included provided the appropriate Thesaurus terms are also used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form requirements for Executive orders and proclamations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed Executive orders and proclamations must have a suitable title; contain a citation of the authority under which issued; conform to the GPO Style Manual; use geographic name spellings per the Board on Geographic Names; land descriptions should follow Bureau of Land Management specifications; and adhere to specified pagination, margins, and spacing (typewritten on approx. 8 x 13 inches, left margin ~1.5 inches, right margin ~1 inch, double-spaced except quotations/tabulations/land descriptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proclamations issued by the President shall conclude with the prescribed recitation ('IN WITNESS WHEREOF...' wording and dating).

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and approval process for drafts of Executive orders/proclamations
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed Executive order or proclamation shall first be submitted, with seven copies, to the Director of OMB with a letter signed by the head or authorized officer explaining nature, purpose, background, effect, and relationship to pertinent laws and other orders/proclamations. If OMB approves, it transmits to the Attorney General for form and legality review; if AG approves, it goes to the Director of the Federal Register for conformity review and transmission to the President if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In urgent cases the Attorney General may transmit directly to the President. If disapproved by OMB or AG, the document shall not be presented to the President unless accompanied by a statement of reasons for such disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and certification of originals and copies of signed Executive orders/proclamations
rubrics_metrics.description: If signed by the President, the original and two copies shall be forwarded to the Director of the Federal Register for publication. The OFR shall place a notation on copies: 'Certified to be a true copy of the original,' signed by the Director or authorized person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required number of copies are forwarded and certification notation is applied and signed by an authorized OFR representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and routing for proclamations calling for observance of special days/events
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility for preparation and presentation of proposed proclamations for observance of special days/events is assigned by the Director of OMB to appropriate agencies; such proposed proclamations must be submitted at least 60 days before the date of observance. Approved commemorative proclamations will be transmitted to the President by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the 60-day lead time and routing procedures notwithstanding other routing provisions (§ 19.2 note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope exclusion for treaties and international agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations do not apply to treaties, conventions, protocols, or other international agreements, or proclamations thereof by the President, consistent with 44 U.S.C. 1511.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat treaties and similar instruments as subject to these document-preparation and publication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Presidential proclamations and Executive orders'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term includes such attachments thereto as are referred to in the respective proclamations or orders, unless the President or representative directs otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include referenced attachments with the proclamation/order unless otherwise directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and role of liaison officers for the United States Government Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified agencies must appoint an officer to maintain liaison with the Office on matters related to the Government Manual. Liaison officers will ensure agency compliance with part 9 and part 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable entities include agencies of the legislative and judicial branches, executive agencies lacking a §16.1 liaison or desiring an additional Manual liaison, quasi-official agencies represented in the Manual, and other agencies the Director believes should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and submission of agency statements for the Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall, according to schedules established under § 20.7, submit for publication in the Manual an official draft of the information required by § 9.2 of this chapter and part 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the schedules and content requirements set out in the referenced provisions; consult OFR for formatting and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization content and presentation in the Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about lines of authority and organization may be reflected in a chart if the chart clearly delineates the agency's organizational structure. Charts must be legible when reduced to Manual page size. Listings of heads of operating units should reflect relationships between units. Narrative descriptions duplicating charts or lists will not be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare charts and listings so they remain legible after reduction; avoid redundant narrative reproducing chart/list information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of program activities for the Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions should clearly state the public purposes the agency serves and the programs that carry out those purposes. Descriptions of responsibilities common to most agencies will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on agency-specific public purposes and program descriptions useful to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of information for agency statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pertinent sources of information useful to the public (employment, consumer activities, contracts, small business services, etc.) should be provided with each agency statement, plainly identifying where the public may obtain information or make submittals or requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear contact points and information sources in agency Manual statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, style, arrangement, and apportionment of Manual space
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register determines the form, style, arrangement of agency statements and the apportionment of space in the Manual. The U.S. Government Printing Office Style Manual is the applicable reference for style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow OFR direction and GPO style for Manual submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline compliance for Manual submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must comply with deadline dates established by the Director of the Federal Register for transmittal of statements and verification of proofs. Failure may result in publication of outdated statements or omission of important material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely compliance preserves the public's right to expect up-to-date information in a particular Manual edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting documents subject to codification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency that prepares a document subject to codification shall draft it as an amendment to the Code of Federal Regulations in accordance with this subchapter, and include words of issuance and amendatory language that precisely describe the relationship of the new provisions to the Code before submitting to OFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft as codification amendments with clear amendatory language to facilitate accurate incorporation into the CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of expiration of codified material
rubrics_metrics.description: When a codified regulation expires after a specified period by its own terms or by law, the issuing agency must submit a notification document for publication in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely publish notices of expiration to keep the public record accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles and subtitles organization of the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles bring together broadly related Government functions. Subtitles may distinguish materials from an overall agency and components or group chapters within a title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use titles and subtitles to group related regulatory material logically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter and subchapter assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters are normal divisions of a title assigned to agencies within a title descriptive of subject matter. Subchapters may group related parts within a chapter. Chapter and subchapter assignments are made by the Office of the Federal Register after agency consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult OFR on chapter/subchapter placement for consistency within a title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts, subparts, and undesignated center heads usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts are normal divisions of a chapter and consist of unified regulations applying to a specific agency function. Subparts or undesignated center heads may group related sections within a part or subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these divisions to structure regulatory content clearly and consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections as basic units and internal subdivision
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections are the basic units of the Code. When internal division is necessary, a section may be divided into paragraphs and further subdivided using the lettering/numbering indicated in § 21.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow numbering and paragraph hierarchy to maintain standard organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard organization and numbering of the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code's standard organization and numbering specify titles (Arabic), subtitles (capital letters), chapters (Roman numerals), subchapters (capital letters), parts (Arabic within titles), subparts (capital letters), sections (Arabic within parts as 'part.section'), and paragraph levels (a, 1, i, A, 1, i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the prescribed numbering scheme to ensure consistency across the CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation of numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where related parts or sections are grouped under a heading, numbers may be reserved at the end of each group to allow for future expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve numbers when planning for addition of related material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviations from standard CFR organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deviation from standard CFR designations must be approved in advance by the Office of the Federal Register. Requests must be submitted in writing at least five working days before the agency intends to submit the final rule for publication and include a copy of the final rule document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may allow section number keying to correspond to an agency numbering system only when it benefits both the agency and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document headings for rules/proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rule and proposed rule document submitted must contain the following headings, when appropriate, on separate lines in order: (1) Agency name; (2) Subagency name; (3) Numerical references to the CFR title and parts affected; (4) Agency numbers/identifying symbol in brackets, if used; (5) Brief subject heading describing the document. Each CFR section in regulatory text must have a brief descriptive heading preceding the text on a separate line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these required headings to provide clear identification and indexing for each document and section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables of contents for parts
rubrics_metrics.description: A table of contents must be used at the beginning of a part whenever a new part is introduced, an existing part is completely revised, or a group of sections is revised/added and set forth as a subpart or grouped under a center head. The table follows the part heading and precedes the text, listing subparts, center headings, sections, and appendix headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include complete lists of headings to facilitate navigation and codification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of part headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each part heading shall indicate briefly the general subject matter of the part. Phrases not descriptive of subject matter (e.g., 'Regulations under the Act of July 28, 1955') may not be used. Introductory expressions like 'Regulations governing' or 'Rules applicable to' may not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part headings should be concise and descriptive of content, avoiding boilerplate or vague introductory phrases.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirements for amendatory documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each amendatory document shall identify in specific terms the unit amended and the extent of the changes made. The number and heading of each section amended must be set forth in full on a separate line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise identification of amendments to ensure accurate codification and public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to the Code and acceptable cross-reference exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: References to the CFR must specify titles, chapters, parts, sections, and paragraphs; ambiguous references such as 'herein' or 'above' are not allowed. Documents referencing material published in the Code must include the Code citation as part of the reference. Agencies shall publish their own regulations in full text; cross-references to another agency's regulations cannot substitute for full publication except in specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions allowing cross-references include court order/statute/reorg plan requirements, references to regulations of an agency with exclusive legal authority applied by another, informational references, references to Federal test/consensus standards that have replaced private standards, and department-level references from a subagency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel citations and historical Code references
rubrics_metrics.description: For parallel references, the CFR and Federal Register may be cited in specified forms (e.g., 'lll CFR lll (lll FR lll). § lll'). When referencing material codified in the 1938 edition or supplements, specific historical citation forms are provided (e.g., 'lll CFR, 1938 Ed., lll').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed citation forms for clarity and historical accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date statements for codified documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document subject to codification shall include a clear statement as to the date or dates upon which its contents become effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide unambiguous effective-date language to facilitate legal and administrative compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display of OMB control numbers in regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: To display OMB control numbers in agency regulations, those numbers shall be placed parenthetically at the end of the section or displayed in a table or codified section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the placement conventions to ensure OMB control numbers are visible and properly associated with regulatory sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation requirements for codified sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section in a document subject to codification must include, or be covered by, a complete citation of the authority under which the section is issued, including general or specific statutory authority delegated by statute and any executive delegations necessary to link statutory authority to the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include complete statutory and delegation citations to establish legal authority for each codified section.
